newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's April c/a deficit narrows to $1.71 bln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's April c/a deficit narrows to $1.71 bln.

text.p: South Korea's current account (C/A) deficit narrowed to $1.71 billion in April from $2.36 billion a year earlier, preliminary figures from the Bank of Korea (BOK) showed on Thursday.
Note: figures are in millions of US dollars

"Exports of heavy industrial goods, especially electronic products, chemicals and vehicles, picked up in April on the strength of recovering global demand," said Paeng Dong-joon, director of the central bank's statistics division.
He said import growth slowed in line with slowing demand in the domestic market.
"The trend of a shrinking deficit looks firm. So we will be seeing the deficit controlled within our earlier target of $18 billion this year," Paeng said.
The BOK figures showed overall heavy industrial exports rose 7.2 percent in April, against a rise of 1.5 percent a year ago.

The central bank said exports of chemicals, including petrochemicals, on a customs-cleared basis rose 19.4 percent in April from a year ago, compared with a fall of 10.2 percent recorded in April last year.
Exports of electronic goods and vehicles rose 6.8 percent and 18.1 percent respectively in April.

Overall imports on a customs-cleared basis rose 1.5 percent in the month, against a 14.3 percent rise a year earlier, the central bank said. Imports of capital goods increased 3.0 percent, raw materials 0.2 percent and consumer goods including foods 2.8 percent.
The central bank said the growth pace of crude imports slowed to 15.9 percent in April from 35.5 percent a year ago.
In the invisible trade account, payments rose to $3.47 billion in April from $3.16 billion a year ago, while revenues increased to $2.59 billion from $2.48 billion.
